targetName: Space Shuttle Discovery launch stack (daylight pad)

terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: multi-body crewed launch vehicle stack (winged orbiter, propellant tank, two solid boosters)
structureKind: bilateral-symmetric about the tank and orbiter plane
materialFamilies: tile thermal protection (matte dielectric, near-black and near-white)
painted metal skin (matte dielectric, soiled off-white)
nozzle liner (matte dielectric, red-brown) — observed, not metal
objectClass.notes: Daylight reference, technicalSuitability pass. See _orbiter/analysis/image-analysis.md. Not a character or hybrid, so no anatomy track applies.

reasoning: Four macro bodies plus a container root. A single-root spec would be shallow by construction.
Occlusion risk drops from the night frame: daylight, and only the base and the far side are hidden.
Every sub-form is a primitive: ogive, cone, cylinder, extruded delta, lofted fuselage.
Repetition is real and now countable: booster ring bands, booster nose thruster ports, cabin windows, elevon panels.
Action readiness is required by the host page, which explodes the stack and makes each component clickable.
Tier stays complex rather than ultra-complex: the subject is a machine of simple surfaces, and ultra-complex is reserved for finish-dominated subjects.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Dark conical cap at the tank apex, distinct from the orange ogive below it.
White rectangular decal on the ogive, offset from the centreline.
Raised conduit running the tank length, with a visible line of fasteners along it.
Fine vertical stringer ribbing over the intertank band, clearly resolved in daylight.
Booster nose is a rounded cone. The night frame suggested a two-slope cone with a step; this reference shows a single rounded profile.
Two black ring bands around each booster, one below the frustum and one lower.
Orange square patch on each booster frustum, below the upper black band.
Clusters of small dark ports on each booster nose cone.
Aft skirt flares strongly, well beyond the case diameter.
Booster nozzle interior is red-brown. Observed colour, not metal.
Near-black nose cap with a hard boundary against the white fuselage.
Cabin window group: three forward panes visible over the nose plus an overhead pair.
Dark marking cluster on the dorsal forward fuselage, bilaterally symmetric. Present and measurable, but this view cannot settle what it is; modelled as an observed marking group.
Thin black band along each wing leading edge, following both sweep angles.
Split lines across each wing trailing edge dividing inboard from outboard elevon.
NASA insignia on the port wing; US flag above the name Discovery on the starboard wing.
Grey streaking and staining across the orbiter white. The surface is used, not clean.

anatomy.note: primaryDomain is object, so no anatomy track applies.

definitionOfDone: Body proportions hold the measured longitudinal landmarks, in particular the 10.45 m offset between the tank apex and the booster apexes.
All four macro bodies are separate, named, clickable and explodable, and carry the host page group names.
Each of the seventeen detail-inventory entries is realised as geometry or a material override.
Marking layout matches the reference: NASA insignia to port, flag and name to starboard.
The model holds up from at least four viewpoints, including two the reference never shows.
Every unobserved region is reported as inference rather than presented as measured.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

featureGroups.name: Longitudinal landmark placement
qualityCriteria: Booster apexes sit 10.45 m below the tank apex.
Orbiter nose sits 16.54 m below the tank apex.
The wing first exceeds the booster envelope 41.23 m below the tank apex.
failureModes: booster tips drawn level with the tank tip
orbiter placed too high on the stack
wing placed forward of its measured station

featureGroups.name: Booster identity features
qualityCriteria: Rounded nose cone, two black ring bands, orange frustum patch, strongly flared aft skirt, red-brown nozzle interior.
failureModes: plain white tube with no banding
grey metal nozzle

featureGroups.name: Wing insignia layout
qualityCriteria: NASA insignia on the port wing, flag above the name on the starboard wing, both reading across the span rather than along the vehicle axis.
failureModes: insignia mirrored between wings
text rotated to read along the axis

featureGroups.name: Honest reporting of unobserved regions
qualityCriteria: Every region the single view cannot show is labelled inference.
failureModes: far side presented as measured
the forward marking cluster given a false identity

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
wing station delta along the vehicle axis
booster ring band presence and position delta

Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Far side of the stack is unobserved; built symmetric and reported as inference.
Orbiter ventral surface faces the tank and is never visible; from published layout.
Payload bay interior is closed in the reference; modelled as a plain bay.
Booster aft skirts and nozzles pass behind the platform deck, so their lower geometry is inferred.

The glove root of the wing is hidden behind the boosters over its whole span, so it is placed from the published root chord. The station where the leading edge crosses the booster envelope IS measured, at 41.23 m below the tank apex.
The dark marking cluster on the dorsal forward fuselage is observed and measurable but its identity is unresolved from this view; modelled as an observed marking group.
Lateral measurements are about 5 percent compressed by a slight stack yaw. The booster axis is kept at the host page value of 7.0 units rather than the compressed measurement.
Scale anchor is the host page contract, tank radius 4.6 units against a published 4.2 m. The reference independently agrees to 0.9 percent on wing span.

Material extraction passed on all eight regions. Six albedos are accepted as corroborating the independent samples; two are rejected because their crops straddle a boundary (booster paint on a shaded edge, glazing mixed with its white frame).

featureReviews.note: Measured on the render and the reference in model coordinates, not by eye. Booster apex lands at x 19.13 against a measured 19.05, an error of 0.08 units or 7 cm. The station where the wing leading edge crosses the booster envelope lands at x -14.96 against a measured -14.65, an error of 0.31 units or 28 cm. This is the defect the night frame produced and this reference fixed: the booster tips are 10.45 m below the tank tip, not 5.94 m.

Double-delta with the sweep break present as real extruded geometry. Span over booster envelope measures 1.504 on the render against about 1.53 on the reference and 1.441 from published dimensions. The residual is projection: the orbiter sits 6.9 units nearer the camera than the boosters.

All five features from this reference are present and read at review scale: rounded nose cone, two black ring bands, orange frustum patch, strongly flared aft skirt, red-brown nozzle interior. Four of the five were invisible in the night frame.

NASA insignia on the port wing, flag above the name on the starboard wing, both reading across the span. Matches the reference. Two defects were found and fixed here: the insignia were first drawn on opaque canvases and rendered as white rectangles sitting on the wing, and before that they were on the wrong wings.

Nose cap and wing leading edges now read correctly: the leading edge is a thin black line rather than the thick grey band of the first attempt. The dark chine line down each fuselage side, which is prominent in the reference, still does not read at review scale. The two-material loft produces it but the boundary sits too low on the section for this viewpoint to catch it.

Dark tip cap, ogive profile, cable tray and intertank ribbing all present. The ribbing reads coarser than the reference even after going from 32 to 72 stringers. The ogive decal is present but is small enough at review scale to be near the visibility floor.

reviewHistory.summary: Rebuilt from the daylight reference. Landmarks verified in model coordinates rather than by eye: booster apex within 0.08 units and the wing station within 0.31 units of measurement, and three material colours brought within 4 percent of their reference samples over two measured correction passes. Turntable passes across four azimuths with reliable segmentation, multi-angle finds no degenerate view, and all nine host-page component labels are proved to sit inside their named components. The Tier 1 silhouette gate is recorded as skipped rather than passed: the reference is a photograph of a scene whose segmenter keeps 58 percent of the frame, and the port wing tip overlaps the service structure in projection, so no automatic matte separates the vehicle. Three matting attempts are documented in the state file. What still does not match: the dark chine line down each fuselage side does not read at review scale, and the intertank ribbing reads coarser than the reference.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: Overcast-bright daylight from high and slightly to one side; shadows are soft and the shaded sides still carry detail, unlike the night frame.
Strong sky fill. Measurable here, where the night frame had almost none.
Weak separation light off the sea haze.
Daylight reference is not clipped, so exposure can be matched rather than invented.

lightingFromPhoto.groundContact: The stack is shown free-standing on the page, so a soft elliptical ground shadow anchors it. In the reference the platform provides that contact.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: Kept low; the hemisphere fill already carries the sky contribution.

proceduralStrategy: Lathe every surface of revolution from an explicit profile: ogive, aft dome, booster nose, skirt flare, nozzle bells.
Extrude the wing and fin from a planform polygon so the sweep break is real geometry.
Loft the orbiter fuselage across stations rather than stacking boxes.
Instance the repetition systems rather than authoring each copy.
Generate all linework, bands and insignia as canvas textures at runtime; the page must work with no network.
Name every mesh with the host page group ids so the existing layer buttons keep working.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
